# i2s-converter golden vectors
# Generated by an oracle transcribed from the pinned upstream:
#   quants.c:1358 quantize_i2_s        (packing)
#   quants.c:1335 dequantize_row_i2_s  (independent read-back)
# The packing is INTERLEAVED, per the dequantiser and the python
# reshape(nblocks, 4, 32). Upstream's own C quantiser is FLAT and
# disagrees with its own dequantiser; that is a latent upstream bug
# never exercised, because bitnet.cpp consumes pre-packed weights.
# NOT from this project's decoder. Each case: bf16 source, packed
# bytes, scale, and the values the independent read-back produced.
# format:
#   case <n> <packed_bytes> <scale f32 hex> <src bf16 hex...>
#        | <packed C rule hex> | <decoded C rule f32 hex...>
#        | <packed GGUF-python rule hex> | <decoded PY rule f32 hex...>
#        | differ <n bytes the two rules disagree on>
# Sizes are multiples of 4 by necessity: four elements share a byte and the
# f32 scale begins at offset n/4, so a non-multiple would pack straight over
# the scale. The converter rejects it.
# The two upstream rules are different functions; `differ` records by how
# much, so the test is checking the rule that was asked for and not the
# other one.
